meta.title: Cash Optimization Engine
meta.subtitle: A Game-Theoretic & Predictive Analytics Framework for Pakistan Commercial Banking

useCases.name: Branch Vault Cash Forecasting & Right-Sizing
useCases.objective: Predict each branch's daily cash demand with 95%+ accuracy and set optimal vault opening balances that eliminate both excess idle cash and stock-out risk.
useCases.problemStatement: Branch managers currently set vault cash levels based on experience and conservatism. A branch disbursing PKR 15M/day might hold PKR 50M in the vault. Across 1,500 branches, this over-provisioning locks up PKR 80–120 billion in non-productive cash. At 11% SBP policy rate, this represents PKR 8.8–13.2 billion in annualized opportunity cost.

optimizationTechnique.name: Stochastic Programming + LSTM Forecasting
optimizationTechnique.description: Two-layer approach: (1) LSTM neural network trained on 3–5 years of daily branch transaction data with features including day-of-week, salary cycles, Islamic calendar, crop cycles, and macro signals outputs a probability distribution of daily cash demand. (2) Two-stage stochastic program where Stage 1 decides vault opening balance and Stage 2 recourses after observing actual demand.

gameTheory.mechanism: Cash Efficiency Score (CES) KPI in branch manager performance scorecard
gameTheory.explanation: Branch managers hoard cash to avoid stock-outs. Treasury wants to minimize idle cash system-wide. Solution: scoring mechanism rewarding proximity to model-recommended vault level, plus Treasury guarantees emergency CIT within 4 hours.

impact.mechanism: Reduce average vault idle cash from PKR 35M to PKR 15M per branch → release PKR 30B aggregate → repo/T-bill at 11%

fsdmEntities.usage: Daily vault cash position tracking per branch
Historical deposit/withdrawal patterns for LSTM training
Branch master data — type, region, capacity
Islamic calendar events, salary cycles, crop seasons

outputs: 7-day cash demand forecast with confidence intervals

useCases.name: ATM Cash Replenishment Optimization
useCases.objective: Optimize ATM cassette loading using reinforcement learning to minimize cash-in-cassette float while maintaining service levels above 98%.
useCases.problemStatement: With 2,000+ ATMs, banks load an average of PKR 4M per cassette with a 40–50% idle rate between replenishments. This locks PKR 3–4B in zero-yield float across the ATM network. CIT trips cost PKR 15,000–25,000 each, with 200+ daily trips often based on fixed schedules rather than demand patterns.

optimizationTechnique.name: Inventory Theory (s,S Policy) + Reinforcement Learning (DQN)
optimizationTechnique.description: Deep Q-Network agents learn optimal replenishment policies through trial-and-error interaction with a simulated ATM environment. The agent balances the cost of a CIT trip against the opportunity cost of excess cash and the penalty of a stock-out (ATM downtime). Inventory theory provides the baseline (s,S) policy that RL improves upon.

gameTheory.mechanism: Performance-based CIT contracts with shared savings
gameTheory.explanation: Bank sets the replenishment schedule (leader); CIT provider optimizes routes given the schedule (follower). Performance-based CIT contracts with penalties for missed SLAs and bonuses for efficiency gains create aligned incentives.

impact.mechanism: Cassette float reduction (30–40%) redeployed to overnight instruments + CIT trip savings (fewer trips × PKR 15–25K per trip)

fsdmEntities.usage: ATM device master data — location, type, capacity

useCases.name: Inter-Branch Cash Netting & Routing
useCases.objective: Create an internal cash market where surplus branches supply deficit branches directly, reducing dependency on central vault and CIT logistics.
useCases.problemStatement: On any given day, 30–40% of branches have surplus cash while 20–25% face deficits. Currently, surplus branches return cash to central vault via CIT, and deficit branches order from central vault — creating redundant, expensive round-trips. Direct branch-to-branch transfers could save PKR 560–760M annually.

optimizationTechnique.name: Network Flow (Min Cost) + VCG Auction
optimizationTechnique.description: Minimum-cost network flow optimization matches surplus branches to deficit branches, minimizing total CIT transportation cost. VCG (Vickrey-Clarke-Groves) auction mechanism ensures truthful reporting of cash surpluses/deficits by making it individually rational for each branch to report honestly.

gameTheory.mechanism: Internal cash market with VCG pricing
gameTheory.explanation: Branches may misreport surpluses to avoid lending. VCG mechanism makes truthful reporting a dominant strategy — each branch pays/receives the externality it imposes on the network, ensuring honest participation.

impact.mechanism: Eliminate redundant CIT round-trips + reduce central vault throughput by 25–35%

useCases.name: CRR Float Engineering & Regulatory Arbitrage
useCases.objective: Exploit SBP's weekly CRR averaging provision to minimize idle reserves while maintaining 100% compliance, unlocking PKR 800M–1.2B in deployable float.
useCases.problemStatement: SBP requires banks to maintain a Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) of 5% of time & demand liabilities, calculated as a weekly average. Most banks hold a flat buffer above the minimum daily. By strategically varying daily CRR balances (high early in the week, lower later), banks can free up significant float for overnight deployment without violating the weekly average requirement.

optimizationTechnique.name: Dynamic Programming + Chance-Constrained Programming
optimizationTechnique.description: Dynamic programming optimizes the daily CRR balance trajectory over each reporting week. Chance-constrained programming ensures the probability of violating the weekly average stays below a threshold (e.g., 0.1%), accounting for uncertain deposit flows that affect the liability base.

gameTheory.mechanism: Conservative CRR band usage to maintain regulatory trust
gameTheory.explanation: Aggressive CRR manipulation risks regulatory scrutiny. In this repeated game, the bank uses a moderate strategy — staying well within legal bounds — to maintain SBP's trust. Tit-for-tat: if SBP signals concern, the bank immediately reverts to flat CRR.

impact.mechanism: Weekly CRR averaging arbitrage releases PKR 7–11B in deployable float at 11% policy rate

fsdmEntities.usage: SBP CRR requirement parameters and thresholds
SBP policy rate and money market rates

useCases.name: Nostro Account Balance Optimization
useCases.objective: Optimize foreign currency nostro account balances across 15–20 correspondent banks to minimize idle FX balances while meeting settlement obligations.
useCases.problemStatement: Pakistani banks maintain nostro accounts in USD, EUR, GBP, AED, CNY and other currencies with correspondent banks globally. Conservative treasury management keeps excess balances to avoid overdraft fees and failed settlements. Across all nostro accounts, PKR 4–8B equivalent sits idle, earning sub-market rates or zero return.

optimizationTechnique.name: Multi-Currency Portfolio Optimization + MDP
optimizationTechnique.description: Markov Decision Process models the state of each nostro account (balance, expected inflows/outflows, FX rates) and finds the optimal rebalancing policy. Portfolio optimization across currencies considers correlation structure, settlement timing, and correspondent bank fee schedules.

gameTheory.mechanism: Explicit fee model replacing implicit balance requirements
gameTheory.explanation: Correspondent banks prefer high nostro balances (free funding). The bank wants minimal balances. Nash bargaining solution: negotiate explicit fee schedules that replace implicit balance requirements, making the true cost transparent and optimizable.

impact.mechanism: Reduce idle FX balances by 30–50% across nostro accounts and redeploy to FX forwards/swaps

fsdmEntities.usage: Nostro account agreements with correspondent banks
FX rates and money market benchmarks

outputs: Optimal nostro balance per currency per correspondent

useCases.name: Vostro Account Liability Optimization
useCases.objective: Optimize vostro account management to reduce liability cost while maintaining reciprocal correspondent banking relationships.
useCases.problemStatement: Foreign banks maintain vostro (PKR) accounts at Pakistani banks. These represent low-cost funding but also operational overhead. Sub-optimal vostro management means paying implicit returns on idle foreign bank balances or losing correspondent relationships. Managing PKR 15–25B in vostro liabilities efficiently can yield PKR 75–250M in annual value.

optimizationTechnique.name: Liquidity-at-Risk (LaR) Framework
optimizationTechnique.description: LaR framework quantifies the probability distribution of net vostro flows, identifying the minimum balance needed to service correspondent obligations at a given confidence level. Excess above LaR threshold is redeployed into higher-yielding PKR assets.

gameTheory.explanation: Both parties benefit from stable correspondent relationships. Cooperative iterated game: bank offers competitive PKR rates on vostro balances in exchange for favorable nostro terms abroad. Defection (cutting rates unilaterally) risks losing the correspondent relationship entirely.

impact.mechanism: Optimize vostro liability cost through better fund deployment and reciprocal rate negotiations

fsdmEntities.usage: Vostro account agreements with foreign banks
PKR money market rates for deployment

useCases.name: Denomination Mix Optimization & SBP Penalty Avoidance
useCases.objective: Optimize the denomination mix (PKR 10 to PKR 5,000 notes) across all branches to minimize SBP soiled note penalties and customer complaints while reducing sorting/handling costs.
useCases.problemStatement: SBP imposes penalties for banks that circulate soiled notes or fail to meet denomination mix requirements. Banks spend PKR 200–400M annually on note sorting, SBP penalties, and denomination mismatches (too many large notes in rural branches, too few in urban). Multi-objective optimization can simultaneously minimize penalties, sorting costs, and customer wait times.

optimizationTechnique.name: NSGA-II Multi-Objective Optimization
optimizationTechnique.description: Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) optimizes three competing objectives simultaneously: (1) minimize SBP soiled note penalties, (2) minimize denomination mismatch costs, (3) minimize note sorting/handling costs. Pareto frontier reveals tradeoffs for management decision-making.

gameTheory.mechanism: Robust denomination plan minimizing worst-case regret
gameTheory.explanation: Customer denomination demand is uncertain (nature). Bank uses minimax regret to find the denomination mix that minimizes the maximum possible regret across all demand scenarios — a robust strategy that performs reasonably well regardless of actual demand patterns.

impact.mechanism: Reduce SBP penalties by 60–80%, lower sorting costs by 25–35%, eliminate denomination mismatches

fsdmEntities.usage: SBP note quality and denomination requirements

outputs: Optimal denomination mix per branch type

useCases.name: CIT Route Optimization & Dynamic Scheduling
useCases.objective: Optimize Cash-in-Transit vehicle routing to minimize total logistics cost while meeting all branch and ATM replenishment time windows.
useCases.problemStatement: CIT operations involve 50–80 armored vehicles making 200+ trips daily across metropolitan areas. Fixed routes and schedules lead to 25–40% deadhead (empty return) mileage. Dynamic routing considering traffic, security zones, and time windows can reduce fleet requirements by 15–20% and CIT costs by PKR 300–600M annually.

optimizationTechnique.name: VRPTW + ALNS Metaheuristic
optimizationTechnique.description: Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) formulation with Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) metaheuristic. ALNS iteratively destroys and repairs solutions using multiple operators (Shaw removal, worst removal, greedy insertion, regret insertion), adapting operator selection probabilities based on recent performance.

gameTheory.mechanism: Shapley value cost sharing across routes
gameTheory.explanation: Multiple CIT vehicles form coalitions to serve overlapping regions. Shapley value fairly allocates the cost savings from route sharing — each vehicle's cost share equals its average marginal contribution across all possible coalition orderings.

impact.mechanism: Reduce CIT fleet size by 15–20%, eliminate 25–40% deadhead mileage, dynamic scheduling

useCases.name: Digital Channel Incentivization & Cash Demand Deflection
useCases.objective: Use mechanism design and adaptive experimentation to shift customer transactions from cash to digital channels, reducing physical cash demand by 15–25%.
useCases.problemStatement: Pakistan's cash-to-GDP ratio of 12–14% is among the highest globally. At branch level, 60–70% of transactions are still cash-based. Each cash transaction costs the bank PKR 35–50 in handling, while digital transactions cost PKR 3–8. Shifting even 15–20% of cash volume to digital channels saves PKR 750M–2B annually and reduces cash cycle costs.

optimizationTechnique.name: Mechanism Design + Multi-Armed Bandit (Thompson Sampling)
optimizationTechnique.description: Mechanism design creates incentive-compatible offers (cashback, fee waivers, lottery entries) that make digital adoption individually rational for customers. Thompson Sampling multi-armed bandit continuously experiments across incentive variants, learning which offers drive the highest conversion rate per customer segment.

gameTheory.explanation: Customers adopt digital channels only if the perceived benefit exceeds switching costs. Bank designs incentive mechanisms that are incentive-compatible (customers' best response is to adopt digital) and individually rational (customers are at least as well off). Thompson Sampling adapts offers in real-time.

impact.mechanism: Shift 15–25% of cash transactions to digital → reduce cash handling cost from PKR 35–50 to PKR 3–8 per transaction

useCases.name: Integrated Cash P&L Attribution & Branch Profitability
useCases.objective: Build a full activity-based costing model for cash operations, enabling transfer pricing and branch-level profitability measurement for all 10 use cases.
useCases.problemStatement: Banks cannot measure the true cost of cash at a branch level. Cash handling costs are buried in operational budgets. Without accurate attribution, branch managers have no visibility into whether their cash management is profitable or destroying value. UC-10 is the measurement and attribution layer that makes UC-01 through UC-09 accountable.

optimizationTechnique.name: Activity-Based Costing + Transfer Pricing Engine
optimizationTechnique.description: ABC model identifies 25+ cash-related activities (vault management, CIT coordination, note sorting, ATM replenishment, etc.) and allocates costs to branches based on activity consumption. Transfer pricing engine charges branches for cash usage above optimal levels and credits them for surplus deployment.

gameTheory.explanation: Branches compete in a tournament where the most cash-efficient branches earn transfer pricing credits. This creates effort equilibrium — branches invest optimal effort in cash management because the marginal cost of improving efficiency equals the marginal tournament prize.

impact.mechanism: Measurement layer enabling PKR 7.8–12.7B attribution across all use cases — no direct savings but enables accountability for UC-01 through UC-09
